title: How a Robin Changes Its View From Fence to Reeds
caption:
How a Robin Changes Its View From Fence to Reeds — five-minute wild observations in just forty seconds. #WildVox #Animals #Nature #Wildlife

narration_timeline.text: On this garden fence, a small European robin sits still, with its bright chest facing the camera.
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic European robin perched on a garden fence; no feeding claimed

narration_timeline.text: Another robin appears on a winter park perch, even when trees offer little cover.
narration_timeline.scene: Real European robin on a winter park perch in Ljubljana

narration_timeline.text: Spring footage shows the same species pausing on low branches and looking across its surroundings.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual European robin on a separate spring park perch

narration_timeline.text: By summer and autumn, other robins appear among leaves in different city parks.
narration_timeline.scene: Two separately filmed robin park clips in June and September

narration_timeline.text: Then the scene changes: two robins perch among reeds and begin to sing.
narration_timeline.scene: Two authentic reed-perched European robins in genuine singing recordings

narration_timeline.text: That orange chest and bright song can turn an ordinary walk into a little birdwatching moment.
narration_timeline.scene: European robin visibly singing in original Flickr footage
